podcast.body: Orbison heard this song, written by his classmates Dick Penner and Wade Moore, at university. It became a successful song for The Teen Kings. After an initial rejection by Columbia and a release on Jewel, Sam Phillips voided Orbison's Jewel contract and re-recorded it for Sun, where it reached number 59 on the pop charts and sold around 200,000 copies. "It soon entered the set of the newly named Team Kings and became one of their most successful songs."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 42: "Ooby Dooby" by Roy Orbison and the Teen Kings

podcast.body: Orbison's sole minor hit on Sun Records. He was signed to the label with The Teen Kings as a rocker-billy singer, despite his personal desire to be a ballad singer. "He had one minor hit on Sun, Ruby Doobie."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
